In recent weeks, ChatGPT users were only subject to weekly usage caps, but OpenAI today (the 25th) announced the resumption of the five-hour usage limit for Plus subscribers on Codex and ChatGPT Work. Details are as follows.

ChatGPT Plus subscribers to see the return of a five-hour usage cap

OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT engineering lead Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux announced this evening (the 25th) that starting tomorrow (the 25th), the five-hour usage limit for Plus subscribers on Codex and ChatGPT Work will be reinstated.

After users hit the five-hour or weekly usage cap, they can wait for the next cycle for usage to reset, or purchase additional credits. OpenAI will also occasionally reset user usage for free, with stored reset opportunities available through designated promotional activities and referral offers.

However, over the past few weeks, OpenAI had temporarily lifted the five-hour usage limit on Codex and ChatGPT Work, retaining only the weekly cap.

During that period, the company also repeatedly reset user weekly usage ahead of schedule to celebrate milestones, including adding another one million active users across the two (now merged) platforms.

However, as Tibo explained on X this evening (the 25th):

"Tomorrow we will be reinstating the five-hour limit for Plus accounts on ChatGPT Work and Codex. I mentioned this earlier and then postponed it. It needs to happen because (a) the five-hour limit helps us spread our compute load and keep the plan generous on the weekly side; (b) the majority of Plus plan users are more casual and newer users who sometimes unknowingly blow through their entire week's usage and then feel confused—the experience isn't great. Over the coming months, the Pro $100 and Pro $200 subscriptions will remain without the five-hour limit."

Tibo made no mention of any changes to Enterprise or Edu accounts, which currently operate on a separate credit-based usage system.

Does the return of the five-hour limit on ChatGPT Work and Codex affect you? Let us know in the comments.
